summary: Frédéric-Guillaume Bergmann was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the universities of Strasbourg, Paris, Göttingen, and Berlin. He spent his career at the University of Strasbourg, serving as professor from 1840 to 1877.

Frédéric-Gustave Eichhoff worked in linguistics and Indology. After earning his Ph.D. at the University of Paris, he taught at the Sorbonne (1837–1838) and served as professor of foreign literature at the University of Lyon (1842–1855).
Fu Yan was a scholar of philosophy and sinology. He studied at the Royal Naval College (~1877–1879) and held posts at Fudan University (~1905–1906) and Peking University (~1912).

Fu-shih Lin specialized in sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He completed graduate studies at Princeton University under Ying-shih Yü, Denis Twitchett, and Stephen F. Teiser (~1988–1994), subsequently holding a post at Academia Sinica (~1994–2021).

Fuguan Xu was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Meiji University and under Shili Xiong (~1943). He later held an academic post at Tunghai University (~1955–1969).

Fuhui Zhang works in linguistics, Tibetology, and history/archaeology. He earned a PhD at Northeast Normal University (2013–2018), where he was also a professor in 2004, and held an attested post at Tianshui Normal University (2012).
Fujio Oda is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Kyushu University. He has held academic posts at Fukuoka University and Beppu University.

Fujio Taniguchi specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Nagoya University under Musashi Tachikawa, studying also with several other teachers, and is affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Fulgence Fresnel worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (~1821–1826) as well as at the Pontifical Maronite College in 1826.

Fumi Yao is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She received her PhD from the University of Tokyo (-2011), where she became an associate professor in 2023, and is affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Fumihiko Sueki specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Yoshiro Tamura, Kyosho Hayashima, and Hajime Nakamura, later serving there as professor (1995–2009) and at Nichibunken (~2009–2015).
Fumihiro Okada works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 2015) and holds an attested post as associate professor at Minobusan University (2026).

Fumimaro Watanabe specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University and the University of Toronto under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Hammalawa Saddhatissa. He served as professor at Kindai University (1981) and Aichi Gakuin University (1987).
Fumio Enomoto is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He worked as a research assistant at Kyoto University (~1980–1985) and served as a professor at Osaka University (~2000–2017).

Fumio Masutani was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar educated at the Fifth Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and Taisho University, and served as president of Tsuru University.

Fumio Matsuda is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Komazawa University and served as an executive committee chairman for the Association for the Study of Indian Religions in 1997.

Fumio Ouchi works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history/archaeology. He obtained his doctorate from Otani University, where he served as an assistant professor (~1993–2000) and later as a professor (~2000–2013).
Fumio Shoji is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University (~1997–2007) and later served there as an assistant professor (~2013–2018) and associate professor (~2018).
Fumio Tamamuro is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He completed his studies at Meiji University (~1954–1964) and later held an academic post there (~1974–2006).

Futoshi Omae is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts as a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1990–1991), Shimane Prefectural Junior College of Nursing (attested 1997), and Shimane International Junior College (attested 1998).
